title: One file per pickup day
prompt: Analysts read the trips one day at a time. Finish `write_table` and `compact` so the table is partitioned by the day each trip was picked up, and each day ends up as a single file. `layout` reports each day's files from the log.
rules: Partition the table by a `pickup_date` column: the date of `pickup_at`. A trip with no pickup time is in a partition of its own.
After `compact`, every day's trips are in one file, and every trip is in the table.
hints: Run the starter and look at `layout`: with no partition column, every file lands under `None`.
`F.to_date` gives the date of a timestamp. Add it with `select("*", ...)` and name it with `alias`, then write with `partitionBy`.
The feed comes in three parts, so a day can start with three files. OPTIMIZE packs each partition's files together.
explanation: Add the day with `select("*", F.to_date("pickup_at").alias("pickup_date"))` and write with `partitionBy("pickup_date")`. The feed's three parts each write a file for every day they hold, so a day starts with up to three files; `optimize().executeCompaction()` packs each partition's files into one, a day at a time. The trip picked up at 23:48 belongs to the day it started, even though it ends after midnight: partitioning by `dropoff_at` moves it to the next day. A trip with no `pickup_at` gets a NULL date, which Delta keeps as a partition of its own. Repartitioning by `pickup_date` before the write also gives one file per day without a compaction; both are fine.
